label: Claude Code presents one skill surface with two invocation paths: Claude uses skills when relevant, or the user invokes one directly with /skill-name; model invocation is the default.

Claude Code exposes run-or-ask as skill frontmatter: disable-model-invocation true prevents automatic loading for side-effect workflows, and user-invocable false hides a skill from the user while keeping it model-invocable.
The Agent SDK documentation states skills are model-invoked and user-invoked: Claude autonomously chooses based on context, or the user dispatches directly by sending /<name>.

Claude Code merged custom commands into skills: a command file and a skill both create /deploy, and existing command files keep working while skills add supporting files, invocation control and automatic loading.
Codex deprecated custom prompts in favor of skills: custom prompts required explicit invocation and were not repo-shared, while skills can be invoked explicitly or implicitly.
Codex's durable instruction layer is AGENTS.md, described as persistent project guidance for every session and the portable place for repo rules.

The ChatGPT desktop app lists skills in the slash menu, allows explicit skill invocation, and exposes custom prompts as /prompts:<name>; the industry pattern is a model-invocable package plus a persistent instruction file.

The repository should mirror the platform pattern: command metadata carries an invocation policy equivalent to disable-model-invocation, the command document is the workflow body, and the brief only names the command and its policy.

Host frontmatter is platform-specific: Claude Code reads .claude skill frontmatter while OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Devin and DSH do not, so a repo-level policy must live in repository metadata and be rendered by the advisor.
